The manipulation of time in the story is carefully balanced to serve its mood and themes. The author effectively uses **compression** to establish the narrator's background and aimless state of mind, summarizing four months of unemployment and a couple of days of routine into the first two paragraphs. The long walk home is similarly compressed at the end once the climax has passed. 

Conversely, the author uses **stretching** during the pivotal moments of the afternoon. The walk behind the couple and the time spent waiting in the rain are paced deliberately to mirror the "long loose hours" of the narrator's life and the rising floodwaters. Most notably, time is stretched at the climax when the woman looks out the window at the floating chair; a few seconds of shared observation are drawn out over two rich paragraphs of internal realization and description, giving the surreal moment the emotional weight and suspense it requires.
